questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Milan because I have always been fascinated by Italian culture. Rome was also an option, but I thought it would be nice to stay in a city that didn't have as many tourists. The University of Milan is also known to be a decent place to study law, which of course also factored into my decision.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The information is sparse and it's expected that you figure most things out by yourself. However, there aren't many important deadlines to miss at the university, so the consequences aren't as big as back home at KU.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The international office will at times send you information about how to sign up for courses. However, most of the information I got came from e-mailing them on my own to ask questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It is difficult to find housing in Milan. I highly recommend applying for dorms more than six months in advance and probably closer to a year. As with most destinations there are also scammers looking to take advantage of desperate students. I found my studio through UniPlaces, which has a 24 hour period before transferring money to the landlord after the date of moving in. This gave me some reassurance that I wasn't being scammed.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It will be expensive: probably between 600-1000 euros. Luckily, the metro lines in Milan are pretty good and offer broad coverage, so most areas are easily accessible.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process for the university itself is pretty easy and done through a form online. Registration for courses wasn't really a thing as it is at KU. You can change the courses you attend throughout the semester, you just have to sign up before any tests/exams (at least at law).

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The course catalogue offers descriptions of courses, but as with most foreign universities it can be hard to understand which courses are offered to you.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Again, this registration is not overly formal and it's quite flexible. This is nice, so you don't have to worry about potential time table conflicts.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to see all of the available courses. There can be timetable conflicts, but you can switch courses mid-semester.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The level of teaching was not very tough, so the courses were only as demanding as the effort you put into them.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses are not challenging, but they can still be interesting.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At law there are only lectures for the whole class. Therefore, it mostly resembles a mix og KUs seminars and lectures. The expected class participation varies from course to course.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
LAW, CULTURE AND DEVELOPMENT IN A GLOBAL WORLD
SMART CITIES, ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION LAW
ACCESS TO JUSTICE IN A MULTILEVEL CONSTITUTIONAL SYSTEM
INTERNATIONAL, EUROPEAN AND COMPARATIVE ENVIRONMENTAL LAW
INTERNATIONAL FINANCIAL LAW AND SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: ACCESS TO JUSTICE IN A MULTILEVEL CONSTITUTIONAL SYSTEM was perhaps the most interesting course. The teachers demanded more of the students.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to live at an airbnb in the first week, this was a last minute solution to my difficulties with finding housing.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Gym memberships are more expensive than in Copenhagen. I had to pay 40 euros a month for a cheaper option.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The erasmus network is the main source of social events. The organizers are very enthusiastic and make sure there are weekly events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Nothing in particular, apart from travelling.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Venice during the low-tourist season is a sight to behold. Maybe the highlight of my exchange. Lake Como is also a great place to go, and it's not far from Milan.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Italian culture will be familiar to most Danes who have travelled and there isn't much of a culture shock. The biggest challenge was the surprisingly large number of Italians that barely speak English. This can of course make day to day tasks difficult, so learning a bit of Italian is a big help.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I never really managed to get to know many locals on a personal level. Most of the people you'll get to know will also be exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There is a laid-back attitude to planning and organization. Larger events can, as a result, often be chaotic. I recommend you just go with the flow and assume that things will work out in the end: they often do.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: There is often a very jovial tone, also among strangers. Most often you'll be met with a friendly and joking demeanor. Most Italians are kind and helpfull.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Go there if you like Italian culture
If you're looking for an academic challenge: look elsewhere
Find a dorm EARLY

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get a student metro card (ATM). It's very affordable. This can be done at offices in the major metro stations (Duomo etc.)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The feeling of being able to live and function in a different country where the first language isn't English.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: If you don't live with others you'll have to make an effort to meet people. The erasmus events are great for this.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
